source_evidence.observation: Within a surrounding sequence of i.i.d. random variables sharing a fixed parameter p ∈ (0,1), the Bernoulli assertion is coordinatewise: each individual Xi has value 1 with probability p and value 0 with probability 1−p. The paragraph also recalls E Xi = p and Var(Xi) = p(1−p).

undebatable_constraints: The parameter satisfies p ∈ (0,1) in the stated source context
The probability of value 1 is p
The association of probabilities with values follows the source’s word “respectively”

contract_plain_english: For a fixed p strictly between 0 and 1, saying that an individual variable Xi is Ber(p) means that Xi equals 1 with probability p and equals 0 with probability 1−p. Its expectation is p and its variance is p(1−p). The passage happens to place such variables in an i.i.d. sequence, but independence and identical distribution are sequence-level assumptions, not part of the law of one Bernoulli variable.
